elements.element: Trigger: obligations arise on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason"
"HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance" — the only condition is our own request, which we control

elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
elements.evidence: "for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date"

elements.element: Return of Customer Data within 30 days
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data"

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
elements.evidence: "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" — "commonly used" carries the same sense as "standard", though the playbook word is not used verbatim
"(c) thereafter delete all such Content, user information, customer data and Confidential Information from its systems"
"certify such deletion to the Company in writing"
"within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data"

reasons: The inserted 4.3 supplies every preferred atomic element: expiry/termination trigger, up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return of Content and customer data in machine-readable form, then deletion and written certification.

The "at the Company's request" condition is limited to clause (a) transition assistance and does not qualify the mandatory 30-day data return, deletion or certification, so the recurring request-condition boundary is respected.

Format wording is "commonly used, machine-readable" rather than the playbook's "standard machine-readable"; the official precision check flags the divergence, but the phrase expresses the same non-proprietary interoperable requirement and is at most a wording nuance to note in the rationale, not a material gap. If the drafter wants a verbatim match, changing "commonly used" to "standard" is a one-word fix.

Insertion is a concise new clause for an otherwise silent exit position — no rewrite of the term, notice or Termination Payment mechanics, and no new exceptions or undefined terms (Termination Date, Content, Company and HDI are all defined).
